candidates.headline_hypothesis: Crypto just unhooked from tech stocks: Bitcoin pushed back above $61K while the Nasdaq fell — powered by a rate-cut hint from a man who no longer works at the Fed, and with ETF money still walking out the door.

the_signal_24h.summary: On 2 July 2026 lead cryptocurrencies rose while equities fell: Bitcoin gained ~2% to hold above $61,000 (intraday ~$61,430, +2.7% on the day), Ethereum +~5% to ~$1,696, and Solana +~5% on the day / +~22% on the week after launching a new on-chain governance mechanism. The move explicitly diverged from tech stocks — the Nasdaq fell ~0.8% and the S&P had closed -0.22% on 1 July. Drivers: ex-Fed governor Kevin Warsh's ECB-Forum (Sintra) comments on AI-driven productivity and room for future rate cuts, plus a weak June US payrolls print (+57k). Yet spot Bitcoin ETFs kept bleeding (~$296M in outflows, ~$220M from IBIT), so institutions have not returned.

virality.source_velocity: Covered by The Motley Fool, Yahoo Finance and Coinpedia plus the daily crypto desks through 2 July; a recurring 'why is crypto up today' explainer wave rather than a single breaking bombshell.

the_depth_90d.summary: The 'decoupling' framing is not new to CurAItion's library — it has tracked the thesis since at least March 2026, when Bitcoin Magazine Pro argued the macro environment gave Bitcoin its best chance yet to break correlation with equities. Today is the first time in a while the price action actually matches the thesis.

citations.title: Why I think Now Is Bitcoin's Best Chance To Decouple

curaition_crossref.note: Library has a standing decoupling narrative (Bitcoin Magazine Pro, Mar 2026). Gives the hot take a depth competitors' pure-news write-ups lack.

candidates.why_now: Ex-Fed governor Kevin Warsh's comments at the ECB Forum in Sintra (1 July) on four straight quarters of AI-driven productivity gains and scope for eventual rate cuts, amplified by a soft June payrolls print (+57k), lifted rate-cut hopes and pushed capital toward risk assets — while tech equities fell.
candidates.why_it_matters: Based on the citations above: 'crypto is just leveraged Nasdaq' has been the bear's favourite jibe for years. A day where Bitcoin rises as tech falls is exactly the counter-example bulls have wanted — but the simultaneous ETF outflows say the smart, slow money isn't validating it yet. That tension (retail/technical rally vs absent institutions) is the real story, not the green candle.
candidates.surprise_factor: The rally's named catalyst is a man who isn't even a current Fed policymaker, and it happened while ETF money kept leaving — a decoupling nobody 'official' is funding.
